```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4)
library(depprep)
```

Two monthly series that both have an annual cycle are correlated even when nothing
links them. `depprep` removes the shared slow structure (cycles, trends, persistence)
before the variables are compared.

## Data with known truth

Eight years of monthly data, twelve variables: four persistent (AR(1)), four with an
annual cycle, two with a trend that shifts in the middle, two without dependence.

```{r simulate}
g <- sim_groups(sim_group("persistent", 4, "ar1", phi = 0.9),
                sim_group("seasonal", 4, "seasonal", period = 12),
                sim_group("trend", 2, "trend_shift"),
                sim_group("none", 2, "none"))
sim <- sim_temporal(96, g, R_true = make_R_true(g, "blocks", within = 0.5, between = 0), seed = 2)
```

With your own data, give the times (`time`, numbers in a regular series) to every
function.

## Diagnose and group

```{r diagnose}
sig <- diagnose_variables(sim, nsim = 99)
sig[, c("variable", "ljung_p", "phi", "period", "trend_r2")]
gr <- group_regimes(sig)
gr[, c("variable", "type", "group")]
```

The seasonal period found by the periodogram is recorded in the grouping and used by the
correction.

## Correct and verify

```{r correct}
cr <- correct(sim, gr)
v <- verify(cr, sim, nperm = 49)
v$variables[, c("variable", "removed", "autocor_before", "autocor_after", "residual_structure")]
```

In time, `verify()` tests the residuals of each variable with a Ljung-Box test whose null
is white noise with the same basis removed (residuals on a basis are not exchangeable).

## When you know the cycle

If the period is known (12 months), say so for the seasonal groups; the harmonics are
then searched for that period only, and the other groups keep the automatic choice:

```{r menu}
seasonal <- unique(gr$group[gr$type == "seasonal"])
menus <- setNames(rep(list(basis_menu(term_trend(), term_cycle(period = 12))), length(seasonal)), seasonal)
cr_m <- correct(sim, gr, menu = menus, scope = "groups")
lapply(cr_m$bases[seasonal], attr, "terms")
```

Without `period`, `term_cycle()` takes the period from the periodogram of the group's
variables.

## Whitening

An alternative to removing slow patterns is to filter each group by its autoregressive
model (`mode = "whiten"`); the correlations then are those of the innovations, a
different quantity.

```{r whiten}
round(correct(sim, gr, mode = "whiten")$R[1:4, 5:8], 2)
```
